articles.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
articles.summary: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
articles.summaryTr: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.
articles.articleText: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war' - Published Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans have "said NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections. "We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X. "If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned. Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices. But he insisted that he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran in February. Iran's Supreme Leader said he did not expect US policy to change after the results. Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the Iran war began, released a statement saying anyone who thinks there will be any change from American "hostility towards the Iranian nation" is "gravely mistaken". In an interview with Fox News, Trump said of the midterm results: "I think a part of it was Iran". He went on to say: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that." Speaking separately to the BBC's US news partner, CBS News, Trump said the conflict would end "when I say it ends". In recent weeks, the president has warned that the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran. Also on Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said four oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said two of the vessels were still burning, and two additional tankers had been intercepted, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. It said they were trying to travel through a prohibited southern route in the Strait of Hormuz. BBC Verify has been investigating the IRGC claims, and has not found any evidence that four tankers were destroyed. In a separate incident, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre said a tanker was struck by two unknown projectiles about 14 nautical miles (26km) north-east of Limah, in Oman's Musandam peninsula, on Tuesday evening. No casualties were reported, it added. On Monday, an Indian crew member of a dhow - a wooden sailing boat - was killed in an attack north-east of Limah. Thirteen other crew members were rescued by Omani authorities. The IRCG also reported on Wednesday that its forces had shot down another US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz. It made a similar claim on Monday night, when US officials said the US military had carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft. - US midterms: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night - Published8 hours ago In an interview with the Financial Times ahead of the midterms, Trump suggested he was happy with the state of the conflict, and that he did not consider them to be "really in a war". When asked about what the newspaper described as "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack on Iran this week, Trump said they were "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no need for it". Indirect talks to end the conflict have been stalled for months. President Masoud Pezeshkian maintained on Tuesday that his government had been trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue". "No-one will benefit from this war" if it were to resume, he warned. He also emphasised that Iran's supreme leader had granted the government powers to negotiate "issues that he had previously considered off-limits". Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqai said on Monday that the basis of the current indirect negotiations mediated by Qatar remained a seven-step proposal that Iran submitted in September. But he added that the proposal had been "condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days". The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, was effectively closed after the start of the Iran war due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and the US naval blockade. The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade. Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters. To keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the Strait of Hormuz. Additional reporting by Gabriela Pomeroy Related topics - Published1 day ago

articles.articleText: Poundland owner in crunch talks as retailer's collapse looms - Published Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds will meet the US-based owners of Poundland on Wednesday as the government hopes to save the retailer from collapse. The discount chain is on the brink of insolvency and Gordon Brothers, which bought it for £1 last June, has rejected a takeover bid which could have saved the 12,000 jobs currently at risk. A meeting was due to be held on Thursday but has been brought forward as the scramble to secure a rescue deal for the firm intensifies. Gordon Brothers has previously said Poundland faces multiple economic challenges from rising inflation, increasing staff costs, and "severe levels of shoplifting". Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of the business has not been made. Meanwhile, MPs say they have called in Poundland's owners for questioning to explain their role in the discount retailer's looming insolvency. Liam Byrne, chair of Parliament's business committee, said: "Every report suggests Poundland is a viable, profitable business with a future ahead of it and without good reason to let it crash and burn - and then to break it up and sell it off piece by piece. "We are asking Gordon Brothers to appear before Parliament to explain themselves and tell us just what it is that's preventing them from accepting the fully-funded deal on the table to save more than 12,000 jobs." Business Minister Kate Dearden and union representatives are also meeting Poundland's managing director Barry Williams later today. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its lenders until next Thursday. The meeting comes after a major Poundland supplier has said it will lose millions of pounds if the retailer goes bust. Adam Turner, sales director at Bradford-based Highcrest Retail Brands, said Poundland was one of its biggest customers and its collapse would cost it "a few million" in lost sales. The family owned business mainly sells confectionery to Poundland and turns over about £50m. Turner said the firm becoming insolvent would leave a substantial gap in its balance sheet next year. Highcrest was a "longstanding business that can stomach this", Turner said. But he warned other medium and small suppliers to the retailer have told him that "if Poundland goes under, so do they". This echoes a warning from Poundland founder Steve Smith on Monday that two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, which only work for Poundland, would be directly affected by its collapse. Not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall, he told the BBC on Wednesday. He said he was "amazed" Poundland was being put into administration, pointing to the profitability of the company. "Also, there's two offers on the table from some really good people," he added. "All I'm asking is for Gordon Brothers to see if they can put a deal together." Gordon Brothers said Walsall-based Poundland is "still not cash generative at a sustainable level" because of the economic issues it faces. If Poundland's stores are sold to new buyers, some of the employees may get new jobs on the same premises. However, it is understood that buyers are only interested in about half the stores at present – meaning roughly 6,000 employees would not be re-employed. - Poundland's founder offers to invest in firm - Published2 days ago High stock levels If Poundland goes under, suppliers will be getting "pennies in the pound" back from the administration, he said, which is "very upsetting" – although he still hopes a deal can be done so Poundland can remain solvent. Poundland owners Gordon Brothers will be a secured creditor, which means they are first in line to get their money back, and suppliers "who have done nothing wrong" will take the financial hit. "It's sad. It's a nightmare for us all to be honest with you. It's not just the suppliers, it's the staff at Poundland, some of these guys have been there for many years. "It's from the warehouse staff all the way to the shop staff to everybody within head office. It's a massive ripple effect through the supply chain," he added. Turner said he had no knowledge of whether Gordon Brothers had deliberately timed the process of Poundland going into administration so it could take advantage of having high stock levels, which it can then sell. One of the ways Gordon Brothers makes money is through stock liquidations – selling off stock from collapsed businesses. One insider familiar with the situation told the BBC that the timing of Poundland facing collapse was "odd" – most retailers don't fall over in the run-up to Christmas. Ministers' questions Dearden has said the government doesn't want to interfere with "current ongoing commercial negotiations", but that ministers want "clarity" on the plans for the retailer. "It's absolutely legitimate for this government to ask the business if they're doing everything they can to protect employees and suppliers up and down the country," she added. Dearden told MPs that the government would be ready to help the company's employees if Poundland collapses. The head of Gordon Brothers' European operations reportedly told the government that the firm stood by its stewardship and had given Poundland £85m in additional financing since its purchase in 2025. articles.titleTr: Canton’s CC rises 4% as SEC staff view it as ‘digital commodity’
articles.summaryTr: SEC staff’s no-action letter covers CC earned by running infrastructure and applications, but is not a binding ruling on its legal status.
articles.articleText: Canton’s CC rises 4% as SEC staff view it as ‘digital commodity’ SEC staff’s no-action letter covers CC earned by running infrastructure and applications, but is not a binding ruling on its legal status. Canton Network’s native cryptocurrency rose 4% on Wednesday after the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) Division of Corporation Finance issued a no-action letter stating it views the token as a “digital commodity.” Canton Coin (CC) traded at $0.098 at 10:27 am UTC, but was still down roughly 4.2% over the past week, according to CoinMarketCap. Canton Network is a privacy-focused network that enables banks and financial institutions to tokenize assets, trade and settle transactions across different platforms. In its Tuesday letter, SEC staff accepted the explanation that CC’s value comes from how the network operates and demand for the token, rather than a central team’s efforts to generate profits for holders. The division also said it would not recommend enforcement action over CC’s issuance without securities registration, provided the tokens are created under the conditions described by Canton. In Friday’s letter to the SEC, Canton developer Digital Asset said network participants earn CC by operating infrastructure and applications, with the protocol determining how many tokens they can mint based on their activity. The SEC issued guidance in March distinguishing digital commodities, such as Bitcoin and Ether, from securities. It said these tokens are not themselves securities, although the way they are offered and sold can still be subject to securities laws. The SEC’s response reflects its staff’s position and is not a binding ruling on CC’s legal status. SEC staff previously issued token-related no-action letters to crypto projects, including DoubleZero (2Z) in September 2025 and Solana-native decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) project Fuse in November 2025. Related: NEAR token sinks 7% as proposal to cut annual token issuance passes

articles.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
articles.summary: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.

articles.titleTr: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
articles.summaryTr: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.
articles.articleText: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline - Published South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC). This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes. Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations. Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection. For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended. Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime. At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%. Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral. "What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday. In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support. The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard. We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so. They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services. But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change. "We face many challenges in Alexandra. There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said. Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties. On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road. The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn't vote, even though she is registered to do so. The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision. "It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years," she said. Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker. Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it. The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique. A drive around Gauteng province reveals similar patterns of neglect and disrepair, especially in the townships. South of Johannesburg, Soweto looks marginally cleaner than Alexandra, but residents also complain about service delivery. Mduduzi Makhubo, 45, has lived in Soweto his entire life and he told the BBC of the community's daily struggles with accessing water and electricity. "Every Monday we know we won't have water after 2pm," he said. Makhubo is registered to vote and intends to use his vote to deal with the "arrogance" he says local leaders have towards residents and "change the status quo". These areas offer a small, but important, glimpse into the state of South Africa's local governance. Years of reports by the auditor-general have highlighted the dire state of most of South Africa's 257 municipalities. A recent report only gave 39 clean audits - the highest ranking a public entity can achieve - between 2024 and 2025. None of Gauteng's three metro cities, Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, featured in this list. Earlier this year auditor-general Tsakani Maluleke said Johannesburg "needs ongoing attention". "If we don't that, we are going to continue on this slide where financial health deteriorates [and] where service delivery continues to be compromised, which is what we are living," she told lawmakers. The city has been labelled "effectively bankrupt" due to the dire state of its finances. Dirty streets, unstable electricity supply and persistent water issues have been common for years. Experts the BBC spoke to agreed that all eyes will be on Africa's wealthiest city as well as the country's seven other biggest municipalities, or metros, particularly those in Gauteng when the results come in. The expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it's ever done Of South Africa's eight metros, only three are governed by a single party. In Gauteng, all three metros are governed by coalition governments, with the ANC the largest party. But that might change. Political analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the elections would be a "verdict ... and judgment" on the ANC. "And the expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it's ever done," she said. Several polls point to a continued decline in support for the party in Wednesday's election, contested by over 500 political parties. One, conducted by Ipsos, put the ANC's support at 30%, down from the 46% it got at the last local elections in 2021. The same poll, along with others, points to a slight increase in electoral support for the Democratic Alliance (DA), especially in Johannesburg. Ipsos predicts the DA will garner 25% support in this election, up from 22% last time. DA leader Helen Zille has been vying for the mayoral chain in the city and her unusual campaign has attracted a lot of attention. The former Cape Town mayor has been captured swimming in crater-sized potholes, ziplining over sinkholes and riding into her final rally in the city in a classic BMW 325i, known locally as a "Gusheshe". She believes the DA is the country's best choice for a government, telling local radio broadcaster 702 last week that "towns and cities that work best are under DA governance". Verwoerd, a former ANC MP and South Africa's ambassador to Ireland, predicted that coalitions would continue being the order of the day across Gauteng. These types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic at a local level and the constant change in leadership, usually caused by parties falling out with each other, has affected service delivery in many municipalities. Verwoerd said in her view, the most stable coalitions would be those that replicate what the ANC and DA have done on a national level, where the historic rivals have agreed to share power. Reflecting on Cape Town, she said it was unlikely that the DA would lose control of the municipality. The coastal city is widely considered the country's best-performing metro and has been run by the DA since the late 2000s when it unseated the ANC. Ethekwini, which includes the port city of Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, would be a "different story", Verwoerd said. The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has been projected to perform well in the area but it is unclear if it will secure the outright majority needed to run the metro. Polls suggest it won't and will need partners to form a government. The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election. Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be "very messy" given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA. A confident Zuma, addressing supporters on Sunday, vowed to take control of a number of municipalities after the elections. Another political analyst Dr Levy Ndou echoed Verwoerd's assessment, saying that a coalition between the DA and ANC seemed unavoidable in most metros. "We're not sure whether the arrangement of the government of national unity could have the potential to influence how the metros are going to be run," he said. Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa's elections. Over 29 million citizens are registered to vote, but the turnout, especially among young people, has seen a steady decline. Ndou attributed this to the "calibre" of the candidates campaigning and the lack of visibility of local councillors, who are often the ones elected to lead their neighbourhoods, in election campaigns. South Africa's electoral commission has seven days to announce the results, but parties have 14 days to form a governing structure. Polls suggest it won't and will need partners to form a government. The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election. Verwoerd reflected that while various options were on the table for the party, forming a government would be "very messy" given its refusal to work with either the ANC or DA. A confident Zuma, addressing supporters on Sunday, vowed to take control of a number of municipalities after the elections. Another political analyst Dr Levy Ndou echoed Verwoerd's assessment, saying that a coalition between the DA and ANC seemed unavoidable in most metros. "We're not sure whether the arrangement of the government of national unity could have the potential to influence how the metros are going to be run," he said. Both experts also spoke about the declining voter turnout in South Africa's elections. Over 29 million citizens are registered to vote, but the turnout, especially among young people, has seen a steady decline. Ndou attributed this to the "calibre" of the candidates campaigning and the lack of visibility of local councillors, who are often the ones elected to lead their neighbourhoods, in election campaigns. South Africa's electoral commission has seven days to announce the results, but parties have 14 days to form a governing structure. articles.summaryTr: Zach Pandl highlighted institutional custody safeguards as crypto markets recovered some losses following the record $6.3 billion Binance hack.
articles.articleText: Binance hack may be ‘temporary setback’ for crypto, Grayscale’s Pandl says Zach Pandl highlighted institutional custody safeguards as crypto markets recovered some losses following the record $6.3 billion Binance hack. Binance’s $6.3 billion hack could temporarily hurt confidence in crypto markets but would ultimately lead to stronger security practices across exchanges, according to Grayscale. “It also underscores the importance of institutional custody, such as offered by US-based crypto [exchange-traded products],” said Grayscale’s head of research, Zach Pandl, in a Tuesday report. “These vehicles hold their assets at state-chartered banks and qualified custodians, typically offering offline storage, multi-signature wallets, SOC attestations and insurance policies,” he added. Binance suffered a record $6.3 billion hack Thursday and pledged to cover all customer losses. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea. Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the allegations as “absurd rhetoric.” The hack was followed by a market sell-off, with Bitcoin falling below $77,000 and BNB losing more than 8% over 24 hours by early Friday. By Wednesday, total crypto market capitalization had rebounded 2% over the past 24 hours to about $2.63 trillion, after touching a weekly low of about $2.55 trillion earlier in the day. The recovery left the market about $100 billion below its Oct. 28 level. Bitwise’s head of research, André Dragosch, told Cointelegraph that recent outflows from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds were “related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment.” Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis

articles.title: Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure
articles.summary: Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10.

articles.titleTr: Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure
articles.summaryTr: Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10.
articles.articleText: Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10. Tron founder Justin Sun is seeking $263,821.20 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial and its lawyers, accusing the Trump family-linked crypto company of submitting a misleading court disclosure about its ownership in a legal dispute over his $45 million WLFI token investment. In a federal court filing, Sun and two co-plaintiffs alleged that World Liberty initially listed Florida as its sole citizenship before amending its disclosure nearly three months later to identify 22 individuals and entities in its ownership chain, including those in the United Arab Emirates. “World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were,” Sun said. “When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.” The amended disclosure came six days after a federal judge questioned World Liberty’s bid to move Sun’s claims into arbitration. World Liberty’s lawyers subsequently argued that the company’s UAE citizenship deprived the federal court of jurisdiction because foreign parties were on both sides of the lawsuit. World Liberty Financial did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for comment. Related: Circle shareholder sues Trump, World Liberty and Steve Witkoff over crypto deals In April, Sun sued World Liberty, alleging fraud and the unlawful freezing of his tokens. World Liberty filed a defamation lawsuit against Sun in May, alleging false statements and violations of token-sale terms. Sun denied the allegations. The legal back-and-forth followed a January 2025 agreement by an Abu Dhabi-backed investment vehicle to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million. Sun previously backed the Trump family’s crypto ventures by investing in World Liberty and buying President Donald Trump’s TRUMP memecoin. He topped the token’s leaderboard for a May 2025 dinner with Trump, with holdings valued at about $18.5 million. UAE ownership disclosure prompts jurisdiction dispute In an Aug. 26 email included in the court exhibits, World Liberty’s lawyer Sam Cleveland said his team had “recently” learned of additional citizenship information. He maintained that World Liberty already had UAE citizenship when Sun filed the lawsuit in April. Sun’s lawyers subsequently sought corporate records and testimony about World Liberty’s ownership and when its attorneys learned of the UAE connection. They allege that World Liberty provided limited documentation but declined to explain why its original disclosure omitted that information. According to attorney Edward Moss’s sworn declaration, the $263,821.20 request covers fees for four attorneys’ work opposing arbitration. It excludes other lawyers’ fees and costs related to jurisdictional discovery and the sanctions motion. Sun said Tuesday he plans to refile in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is scheduled for Dec. 10. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball
articles.articleText: Release Number 9314-26 CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball October 26, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the National Basketball Association today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets. Through the MOU, the CFTC and NBA will better share information by regularly communicating and discussing matters relating to integrity, as well as maintaining fair and transparent prediction markets. “I’m pleased the CFTC and NBA signed an MOU which continues the Commission’s commitment to increasing data sharing between the agency and professional sports leagues,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The NBA joins the MLB and NHL in taking a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud. I thank NBA Commissioner Adam Silver for putting the integrity of professional basketball and America’s financial markets first and for working with the CFTC on this MOU.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9313-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud October 21, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana entered a default judgment against defendants Michael B. DePetrillo, Meteor LLC, and NOLA FX Capital Management LLC for their participation in a fraudulent retail forex scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented that participant funds would be used to trade retail forex, made material misrepresentations and omissions regarding the profitability of forex trading with them, and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying DePetrillo’s personal expenses, and trading in DePetrillo’s personal account. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,211,492 civil monetary penalty. The order also permanently enjoins the defendants from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposes permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2024 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9003-24] On Feb. 18, 2025, in a related criminal case, DePetrillo pleaded guilty to violating the Commodity Exchange Act in connection with the same conduct in the CFTC’s complaint. On July 23, 2025, the court sentenced him to nine years in prison and ordered him to pay $6,748,412 in restitution. The CFTC appreciates the assistance of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana and the FBI New Orleans Division. -CFTC-

news.articleText: Fon soruşturması: Eski SPK Başkanı ve Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ifadeye çağrıldı YAYIN TARİHİ, 04 Kasım 2026 18:02 GÜNCELLEME, 04 Kasım 2026 18:04 PAYLAŞ - Sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturmasında yeni gelişme yaşandı. Eski SPK Başkanı İbrahim Ömer Gönül, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya, yarın şüpheli sıfatıyla ifade vermek üzere savcılığa çağrıldı. Sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturması kapsamında, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya ile İbrahim Ömer Gönül "şüpheli" sıfatıyla yarın ifade verecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı Terörizmin Finansmanı ve Aklama Suçları Soruşturma Bürosunca, sermaye piyasalarındaki işlemlere ilişkin yürütülen fon soruşturması devam ediyor. Bu kapsamda, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, İlyas Kaya ve eski Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu Başkanı İbrahim Ömer Gönül yarın "şüpheli" sıfatıyla ifadelerinin alınması için emniyet aracılığıyla savcılığa çağrıldı. news.title: Zelensky awards Melania Trump Ukraine's highest award after Oleshky ceasefire
news.summary: Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet the US first lady at the White House on Thursday.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Zelensky awards Melania Trump Ukraine's highest award after Oleshky ceasefire
news.summaryTr: Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet the US first lady at the White House on Thursday.
news.articleText: Zelensky awards Melania Trump Ukraine's highest award after Oleshky ceasefire - Published Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has given the country's highest award for women to the US First Lady, Melania Trump. The Order of Princess Olga, 1st Class, was awarded to Melania Trump for her "significant personal contribution to humanitarian support for Ukraine", according to the presidential decree. It comes after the end of ceasefire in Ukraine's southern region of Kherson, which allowed for the evacuation of several hundred people from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Russian and Ukrainian delegations - made up of ombudsmen who were involved in the evacuation mission as well as senior officials - are due to meet at the White House on Thursday on Melania Trump's invitation. The White House said that Melania Trump had "independently initiated engagement between the two warring nations and successfully secured a ceasefire". "This achievement marks an unprecedented diplomatic initiative by an American First Lady." it added. Both the Russian and Ukrainian sides repeatedly thanked Melania Trump for brokering the ceasefire, though neither elaborated on the nature or extent of her involvement. The delegations travelling to the White House on Thursday will include Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, as well as Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia and Russian senior official Kirill Dmitriev. Lubinets and Lantratova travelled together into Oleshky last week, in an unusual show of cooperation between Russian and Ukrainian officials. Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads Zelensky's party in parliament, has previously been part of the Ukrainian negotiating team during peace talks with Russia. He was responsible for informal contact between the White House and Moscow during the ceasefire, according to diplomatic sources quoted by Ukrainian media, and has confirmed he will take part in Thursday's talks. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Russian delegation will be made up of Lantratova and Kirill Dmitriev, a Russian businessman close to the Kremlin who has frequently taken part in US-brokered ceasefire talks. Although both Dmitriev and Arakhamia are veteran participants in high-level peace negotiations, meetings involving such senior representatives are rarely convened through an initiative led by a US First Lady. No details of what the White House event will entail have been shared. "There are important meetings ahead," said Lubinets in a social media post while announcing he was on his way to the US. On Thursday Melania Trump will also deliver remarks on the ceasefire in Oleshky at 11:00 (16:00 GMT), the White House website said. Zelensky's decree also cited Melania Trump's wider humanitarian work, including her efforts concerning Ukrainian children affected by the war, as reasons for giving her the Princess Olga award. Melania Trump has largely remained discreet on foreign policy matters, but in 2025 she said an "open channel of communication" had been established with Russian President Vladimir Putin, allowing for Ukrainian children displaced in the war to be reunited with families. Earlier this year the UN said the deportation and forcible transfer of Ukrainian children to Russia constitutes a crime against humanity and a war crime. According to Ukraine, almost 20,000 children have been illegally sent to Russia and Belarus since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russian, Ukrainian and American representatives are also going to meet in Abu Dhabi next week in the first trilateral meeting since February. The talks will be focused on postwar security agreements and de-escalation, US envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.

news.title: AB'de genişleme takvimi netleşiyor: 4 ülke için yol haritası hazırlandı
news.summary: Avrupa Birliği (AB) Komisyonu, Karadağ, Arnavutluk, Moldova ve Ukrayna'nın üyelik süreçlerini hızlandırmak amacıyla yeni yol haritaları hazırladı. Karadağ'ın 2028'de AB'nin 28'inci üyesi olabileceği belirtilirken, diğer aday ülkeler için de müzakere hedefleri açıklandı.

news.summaryTr: Avrupa Birliği (AB) Komisyonu, Karadağ, Arnavutluk, Moldova ve Ukrayna'nın üyelik süreçlerini hızlandırmak amacıyla yeni yol haritaları hazırladı. Karadağ'ın 2028'de AB'nin 28'inci üyesi olabileceği belirtilirken, diğer aday ülkeler için de müzakere hedefleri açıklandı.
news.articleText: AB'de genişleme takvimi netleşiyor: 4 ülke için yol haritası hazırlandı - Avrupa Birliği (AB) Komisyonu, Karadağ, Arnavutluk, Moldova ve Ukrayna'nın üyelik süreçlerini hızlandırmak amacıyla yeni yol haritaları hazırladı. Karadağ'ın 2028'de AB'nin 28'inci üyesi olabileceği belirtilirken, diğer aday ülkeler için de müzakere hedefleri açıklandı. AB Komisyonunun Genişlemeden Sorumlu Üyesi Marta Kos, 2026 Genişleme Paketini Avrupa Parlamentosu Dış İlişkiler Komitesinde sundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Son bir yılda üyelik yolunda en fazla ilerleme kaydeden dört ülkeye yönelik yol haritalarının hazırlandığını belirten Kos, her ülkenin reform performansına göre değerlendirileceğini vurguladı. Karadağ için 2028 hedefi Karadağ'ın 21 müzakere faslını geçici olarak kapattığını açıklayan Kos, kalan fasılların da yıl sonuna kadar tamamlanabileceğini söyledi. Katılım antlaşması üzerindeki çalışmaların başladığını belirten Kos, ülkenin 2028'de AB'nin 28'inci üyesi olma yolunda ilerlediğini ifade etti. Arnavutluk'un ise dört faslı geçici olarak kapattığını aktaran Kos, reformların sürdürülmesi halinde ülkenin üyelik müzakerelerini 2027 sonuna kadar tamamlayabileceğini bildirdi. Moldova'nın 2028 başında müzakereleri bitirme hedefi için reformlarını hızlandırması gerektiğini belirten Kos, Ukrayna'nın da hukukun üstünlüğü, demokratik kurumlar ve kamu yönetimi reformlarına öncelik vermesi gerektiğini söyledi. Yeni entegrasyon modeli 2027'de başlayacak Kos, aday ülkelerin tam üyelik öncesinde AB ile daha fazla bütünleşmesini sağlayacak yeni bir kademeli entegrasyon modeli üzerinde çalıştıklarını açıkladı. Bu kapsamda aday ülkelerle görüşmelerin 2027'nin ilk çeyreğinde başlaması planlanıyor. Diğer aday ülkelerin durumuna da değinen Kos, Sırbistan'da ifade özgürlüğü alanında gerileme yaşandığını, Kuzey Makedonya'nın anayasa değişikliklerini tamamlaması gerektiğini belirtti. Bosna Hersek ve Kosova'da siyasi ve kurumsal sorunların reformları geciktirdiğini kaydeden Kos, Gürcistan'ın AB üyelik sürecinin ise fiilen durduğunu ifade etti.

news.titleTr: SEDDK'den Tera Yatırım açıklaması: İddialar asılsız, hukuki süreç başlatılacak
news.summaryTr: Sigortacılık ve Özel Emeklilik Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu (SEDDK), Tera Yatırım'ın Doğa Sigorta ve Prive Sigorta'yı satın alma sürecine ilişkin ortaya atılan iddiaların gerçeği yansıtmadığını bildirdi. Kurum, itibarını zedelemeye yönelik paylaşımlarla ilgili hukuki süreç başlatılacağını açıkladı.
news.articleText: SEDDK'den Tera Yatırım açıklaması: İddialar asılsız, hukuki süreç başlatılacak - Sigortacılık ve Özel Emeklilik Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu (SEDDK), Tera Yatırım'ın Doğa Sigorta ve Prive Sigorta'yı satın alma sürecine ilişkin ortaya atılan iddiaların gerçeği yansıtmadığını bildirdi. - Kurum, itibarını zedelemeye yönelik paylaşımlarla ilgili hukuki süreç başlatılacağını açıkladı. Sigortacılık ve Özel Emeklilik Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu (SEDDK), fon süreci ve Tera Yatırım'ın sigorta şirketlerini satın alma girişimine ilişkin kurum hakkında ortaya atılan iddialara yanıt verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle SEDDK'den yapılan açıklamada, kamuoyunu yanlış yönlendirme amacı taşıdığı belirtilen paylaşımlardaki iddiaların bütünüyle asılsız olduğu ve hiçbir hukuki ya da fiili dayanağının bulunmadığı ifade edildi. SEDDK'den Doğa Sigorta ve Prive Sigorta açıklaması Açıklamada, kurumun sermaye piyasalarında yaşanan olumsuz gelişmelerde asli rolü bulunan finansal kuruluşların sigortacılık sektörüne girişini engellediği belirtildi. Böylece söz konusu sorunların sigortacılık sektörüne yayılmasının ve diğer alanlarda büyümesinin önüne geçildiği kaydedildi. SEDDK, yanıltıcı paylaşımlarda adı geçen şirketlerde tespit edilen kayıpların büyük bölümünün eylül ayı sonunda gerçekleştiğini bildirdi. Kayıpların eş zamanlı olarak kurumun gözetimine takıldığı, denetime alındığı ve bir haftadan kısa süre içinde raporlanarak ilgili kurumlara ve adli mercilere iletildiği aktarıldı. Açıklamada, ilgili şirketin 30 Ekim 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) gönderdiği özel durum açıklamasında da SEDDK'nin denetim faaliyetleri ve tespitlerine yer verildiği hatırlatıldı. Şirketlerde yeni tedbirler alındı SEDDK, denetim raporu ve kurumun direktifleri doğrultusunda ilgili şirketlerde yatırım politikalarından iç denetim süreçlerine kadar çeşitli tedbirlerin alındığına ilişkin bilginin kendilerine iletildiğini bildirdi. Kurum, mevzuatla belirlenen görev ve yetki alanı kapsamında gerekli işlemlerin gecikmeksizin gerçekleştirildiğini vurguladı. Hukuki süreç başlatılacak SEDDK açıklamasında, kurumun ve sigortacılık sektörünün itibarını zedelemeye yönelik mesnetsiz iddialarda bulunanlar hakkında hukuki süreç başlatılacağı ve bu süreçlerin hassasiyetle takip edileceği belirtildi. SEDDK, ilgili şirketlerde tespit edilen kayıpların büyük bölümünün eylül ayı sonunda gerçekleştiğini ve denetim sürecinin bir haftadan kısa sürede raporlanarak ilgili kurumlara ve adli mercilere aktarıldığını açıkladı.

news.title: Mother of Ghanaian boy killed in US 'wants justice' as she flies for funeral
news.summary: Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Mother of Ghanaian boy killed in US 'wants justice' as she flies for funeral
news.summaryTr: Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys.
news.articleText: Mother of Ghanaian boy killed in US 'wants justice' as she flies for funeral - Published The mother of a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was fatally shot in the United States last week has left Ghana for America after being granted an emergency visa by President Donald Trump. "I want justice for my son," Doris Adu Gyamfi told the BBC at the airport before her departure. She said he had dreamt of becoming a medical doctor. Her son, Javits Frimpong, was chased down and shot on Thursday morning on his way to school in the Bronx, New York. He was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys in connection with the shooting. His death has sparked outrage in both Ghana and the US, and reignited the debate about gun violence in America. His mother was escorted to the airport by relatives and Dr Erieka Bennett, Head of Mission of the African Diaspora Forum. "I'm going to America to plan my son's funeral," Gyamfi said. She thanked the government and well-wishers for their support and prayers following her son's death. In a social media post on Saturday, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said Trump had agreed to grant a visa to Gyamfi so she could mourn her son in person. Mamdani said the murder of a child was a pain no parent should endure, "let alone from thousands of miles away.” "Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately," he said. "All of New York City is mourning this tragedy," he added. Ghana's government has condemned the killing and said it was following the case closely to ensure justice. It has urged US authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and said it was ready to provide legal and consular support to ensure the perpetrators are brought to justice. Police are searching for three teenage suspects who fled the scene, captured on surveillance footage. The shooting has sparked concern among Ghanaians about the safety of children sent to study in America. news.title: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change
news.summary: The cereal giant has changed the recipes for Rice Krispies and Coco Pops, sparking a backlash online.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change
news.summaryTr: The cereal giant has changed the recipes for Rice Krispies and Coco Pops, sparking a backlash online.
news.articleText: Kellogg's admits snap, crackle and pop is quieter after uproar over Rice Krispies recipe change - Published Kellogg's has told the BBC the "snap, crackle and pop" sound made by its Rice Krispies may be noticeably quieter after an uproar over the cereal giant's recipe change. Rice Krispies and Coco Pops are no longer being made with whole rice grains, with the tiny toasted puffs being made using corn flour and rice flour instead. A Kellogg's spokesperson said retaining the iconic sound had been a "huge focus" when designing the new recipe, but that customers "might notice that the sound may be quieter and not as instant as before". It followed an online uproar about changes to the breakfast staples, with some fans saying they had lost the "pop" sound altogether. Kellogg's said the recipe was altered due to "changing weather conditions" that have disrupted supplies of some grains and cereals. The cereal giant said the new versions had been "carefully assessed for taste, appearance and texture", but fans complained online they no longer made the famous "pop" sound and said their children would no longer eat them. Some expressed dismay that the taste and texture were "totally different" and dubbed the change "grim" and "disgusting". "There's no snap, crackle and pop in these," a parent named Dani wrote on TikTok. "My toddler won't eat them." Lauren, also posting on TikTok, added that she had been eating Rice Krispies every day for breakfast "for years and years". "I had a bowl of the new recipe and you can immediately tell the difference," she said. "They don't have the snapping sound when you put in the milk." Jessicake meanwhile said they tasted "weird and stale". The "Snap, Crackle and Pop" - made when milk is added to the puffed rice - has been a centrepiece of the brand's marketing since the 1950s. Kellogg's insisted the snap, crackle and pop is "still there, but consumers might notice that the sound may be quieter and not as instant as before". Recipe changes are notoriously difficult for big brands. Chocolate makers are constantly accused of reducing cocoa content in their products and debates rage online over whether ketchup ingredients have changed. When Scottish fizzy drink Irn Bru cut its sugar content in 2018, fans famously stockpiled crates of the old version. No changes are being made to Rice Krispies products in the US and Canada. Kellogg's said the recipe change in the UK would help "maintain consistent quality" as extreme weather takes a toll on crops and pushes up ingredient prices. Extreme weather in Spain in 2022 and 2023 in particular had reduced availability of the types of rice the company uses for its breakfast cereals, the company said Rice Krispies, launched nearly a century ago, are sold around the world and come in variations such as vanilla and strawberry flavours in some markets alongside the widespread chocolate-flavoured Coco Pops version. "We appreciate that even small changes to a much-loved product can feel noticeable and that's why we have approached this with a lot of care and consideration," Kellogg's said. The firm said it appreciated the customer feedback and would "continue to look at ways to make [its] products even better in the future". The cereals have already undergone some change, with reductions in salt content in the 1990s and lowered sugar in 2018. The company said Rice Krispies and Coco Pops will continue to meet UK food standards on levels of fat, salt and sugar in food. A backlash against processed foods in recent years, especially those low in fibre and high in sugar, has put cereals generally under the spotlight from healthy eating advocates. Kellogg's stressed the cereals contain no artificial colours, flavours or sweeteners and the nutritional benefits in each bowl, such as fibre, Vitamin D and iron are staying the same. However, the new recipes mean packaging will now include a "contains wheat gluten" warning. Previously packaging said the products "may contain gluten" because they were made in a factory handling other cereals and there was a risk of cross-contamination. - Watch: How does El Niño affect world weather? - Published21 August Kellogg's said it has not changed the recipe for any of its other cereals. Many parts of the world have been affected by droughts, floods and heatwaves this year due to the El Niño weather phenomenon. The weather event is expected to severely affect crop production from South East Asia in particular. The region produces more than a quarter of the world's rice. The World Meteorological Agency expects the record-breaking El Niño will last until at least 2027. That will intensify pressure on food manufacturing companies, already looking at ways to source reliable and affordable ingredients. The original Kellogg company separated into two distinct firms in 2023. The largest is Kellanova, which focuses on snacks, cereals, noodles and other food products like Eggo, Pringles and Pop-Tarts sold globally. It is now owned by Mars, which makes confectionery and pet food. The other business, WK Kellogg's, operates in North America and has since been taken over by Italian chocolate giant Ferrero. news.articleText: Avrupa'da siber saldırı dalgası: Bu kez kan bankaları hedefte - Avrupa genelinde soğutma sistemlerine yönelik siber saldırılar kan bankalarına sıçradı. Fransa'da kan ürünlerinin saklandığı soğuk hava depolarının sıcaklıkları bilgisayar korsanları tarafından uzaktan yükseltildi. Yetkililer, saldırıda herhangi bir kan ürününün zarar görmediğini açıkladı. Fransız Kan Kurumu (EFS), pazartesi günü üç tesisindeki soğuk depolama sistemlerinin siber saldırıdan etkilendiğini duyurdu. Kurumun açıklamasına göre, dış hizmet sağlayıcıları tarafından işletilen sistemlere uzaktan müdahale eden bilgisayar korsanları, sıcaklık ve buz çözme eşiklerini aşırı yüksek seviyelere çıkardı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Saldırıdan etkilenen depolarda kan ürünleri, dondurulmuş plazma ve biyolojik örnekler muhafaza ediliyordu. Alarm sistemleri olası zararı önledi EFS, izleme ve alarm sistemlerinin anormallikleri hızla tespit ettiğini, etkilenen ekipmanların kontrol altına alındığını veya devre dışı bırakıldığını bildirdi. Kurum, saldırı nedeniyle herhangi bir kan ürünü ya da biyolojik örneğin kaybedilmediğini, gerekli ürünlerin diğer tesislere aktarıldığını açıkladı. Fransa Sağlık Bakanlığı da durumun kontrol altında olduğunu ve kan tedarikinin güvenliğinin sağlandığını belirtti. news.titleTr: James Talarico becomes first Democrat to win Texas Senate seat since 1988
news.summaryTr: "This wasn't just a tsunami, not just a referendum, but this was a bloodbath," one expert told the BBC on Democrats' historic wins in Texas.
news.articleText: James Talarico becomes first Democrat to win Texas Senate seat since 1988 - Published Democrat James Talarico has won the Senate race in Texas, facing off more than $200m in opposition spending and creating one of the biggest upsets for Republicans in the midterms. Talarico's stunning victory over Republican Ken Paxton marks the first time a Democrat has won a US Senate seat in Texas since 1988 - and helped solidify Democrats taking control of the US Congress in a wave of wins across America. Talarico, a former schoolteacher, was little-known until last year. He made the rising cost of living under Republican leadership a central theme of his run. Paxton sought to portray Talarico's views as too progressive for the state, and campaigned alongside Trump on several occasions. In a further, historic victory for Democrats in the state, Gina Hinojosa will become the first Latina governor in Texas, ousting Republican incumbent Greg Abbott - one of the nation's highest profile governors and a long-standing Trump supporter. At a watch party in Austin, the state's capital, there were jubilant scenes among Talarico supporters as giant television screens projected him the winner on Tuesday night. Supporters hugged, they kissed, and they drank to a reality that many say they dared not believe would come true. Emerging on stage to rapturous applause at his official watch party at a nearby performing arts theatre, Talarico pronounced: "We just took back Texas." "We just proved that all the money in the world is no match for the people of Texas," he continued, referring to his win over Paxton whose campaign was backed by Elon Musk, the world's richest man. He invoked religious themes that have grown familiar to his campaign, comparing his unlikely odds to the biblical story of David and Goliath. "This win, this win is for every Texan who's ever wondered if anyone is listening," he said. "I hear you, we hear you. And tonight the world hears you." For decades, the idea of a Democrat winning a statewide race had felt like a pipe dream for Texas liberals. As the nation's second most populous state, Texas has been a bastion of conservatism, routinely rolling out Republican policies that are later employed elsewhere. But throughout the campaign, polls suggested state legislator Talarico was breaking through with voters, energising a Texas Democratic base desperate for new leadership. Spending in the race skyrocketed, and it quickly grew to become the most expensive US Senate race in history, with more than half a billion dollars spent. Billionaire Elon Musk poured in $158m (£117m) to a super PAC supporting Paxton's campaign - a point that Talarico used in attacks on Paxton's campaign. Speaking to CBS on Wednesday morning after his victory, Talarico said Musk "wanted a senator who was going to do his bidding, who was going to sell off Texas land to his data centers, who was going to give [away] our Texas water". "I think last night the people of Texas delivered a crystal clear message to the world's first trillionaire: Texas is not for sale," he said. Then two members of the Bush family, the Republican political dynasty that counts Texas as its political launchpad, backed Talarico in a stunning move foreshadowing Paxton's doom. George Washington University political science professor Quardricos Driskell told the BBC that Paxton was a major part of Republicans' downfall, calling him an "objectively terrible candidate". He said the win in Texas by Talarico, combined with another upset on Tuesday that ousted the state's Republican governor Greg Abbott, was "absolutely historic". Abbott's loss marked the first time a Democrat had won a race for governor in the state since the 1990s. "This wasn't just a tsunami, not just a referendum, but this was a bloodbath," Driskell said about Democrats gains in the Lone Star State. "A clear distinction that the country wants to go in a different direction". Talarico defeated a well-known opponent, Dallas Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett, in the Democratic primary. Then continued to maintain good polling numbers despite an onslaught of negative adverts, including attacks on past comments where he supported transgender people. Throughout his campaign, he frequently leaned into his religious upbringing – as the grandson of a Southern Baptist preacher who spent time in a seminary – sprinkling his stump speeches with biblical references. Paxton had been beleaguered by a number of political scandals, including his impeachment by his own party in 2023 on corruption accusations, before he was later acquitted by the state's Senate. He was also indicted by the US Securities and Exchange Commission on federal fraud charges, but they were later dismissed. Trump made multiple stops in Texas to beef up support for Paxton and other Republicans - including in reliably-Republican spots, signalling how concerned party leadership was about turnout. Voters have been frustrated with high consumer costs, including the price of petrol, and largely blame Trump's tariff policies and the Iran war. Hispanic voters and those who live along the southern US border have also taken issue with Trump's immigration policies. Despite border crossings plummeting under Trump - something that had been popular with Texas voters - polls suggested Trump's support among Hispanics, who make up a third of the state's population, had ebbed significantly. Surveys taken since late summer indicated a majority of Texan Hispanic voters - many of whom switched to Trump to help him win the White House in 2024 - now disapproved of the president. They also suggested that Hispanic voters were favouring Democrats over Republicans by a significant margin. Many Texas Hispanics who spoke to the BBC before the election pointed to Trump's immigration crackdown as the reasoning behind their change of heart. They pointed to aggressive measures that led to citizens being detained and non-violent offenders being rounded up indiscriminately. Reacting to the result on Truth Social, Trump wrote: "If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn't become a RINO [Republican in name only] in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn't have lost." news.title: Everything you need to know from the US midterm elections
news.summary: Democrats secured some big wins - and a few historic firsts - earning congratulations from President Trump.
