news.titleTr: Everything you need to know from the US midterm elections
news.summaryTr: Democrats secured some big wins - and a few historic firsts - earning congratulations from President Trump.
news.articleText: Everything you need to know from the US midterm elections - Published Democrats have won both the US Senate and House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency. Projected results have provided the party with a number of things to celebrate - and rival Republicans some reasons to commiserate. Here is everything you need to know about some of the big Democratic wins and some historic firsts. Democrats toast victories in deep-red Trump country Democrats have tallied up victories in states that were comfortably won by Trump two years ago in the presidential election. With James Talarico winning a seat in the US Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa being elected state governor, Democrats scored two statewide victories in Texas - ending a string of defeats they have endured for almost two generations. Talarico's supporters went beserk as the projected results arrived at an election-night party, wrote the BBC's Gary O'Donoghue. Attendees hugged, kissed and drank to a reality they dared not believe would come true. Hinojosa became the first Latina to be elected governor of the state. Among the other states where history was made by the Democrats were Kansas, where Adam Hamilton took a closely-fought Senate seat - giving the state its first Democratic senator for nearly a century. Senior party figures who cheered the results included Hakeem Jeffries, the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, who is now poised to take over as the Speaker of the lower chamber of Congress. "Today begins the great American comeback," he told a crowd of supporters. If Jeffries' colleagues choose to keep him as the leader of their party's delegation in House, he will be the next Speaker, taking over from Republican Mike Johnson and becoming the first black person to fill that role. Trump congratulates opposition and acknowledges Iran and fuel prices were issues Trump spoke throughout the evening to a number of US media outlets, striking a conciliatory tone and conceding that the Democrats did a "good job". He said he would accept the results and that he was looking forward to working with the opposition party - albeit he would still have the power, as president, to veto legislation that Democrats advance through Congress. Trump distanced himself from some of the Republican candidates who contested the election, saying: "In some cases they didn't like the candidates, and in some cases those candidates were not my friend." He acknowledged that the US-Israel war on Iran, which has impacted consumer prices in the US, had affected the vote. Trump argued that high fuel prices meant voters could not see how well his economy was doing "as much as they should have", adding: "The gasoline was caused by Iran." El-Sayed wins US Senate race in Michigan after fellow Democrat turns on him Abdul El-Sayed has become the first Muslim person elected to the US Senate - after claiming victory in Michigan in what was one of a handful of closely fought contests. His win means the seat stays in Democratic hands. He defeated Republican opponent Mike Rogers, who received the surprise backing of El-Sayed's Democratic rival in the primary contest, Haley Stevens, who changed her endorsement at the eleventh hour. The race was one of the bitterest of the midterms. Trump invoked 9/11 and even called El-Sayed a "jihadist" without citing any evidence, prompting a backlash and accusations of Islamophobia. El-Sayed's supporters went wild when he took the stage to celebrate his claimed victory, wrote the BBC's Nada Tawfik. He said: "Up until right about now, you might have noticed I always say 'inshallah,' or 'God willing,' whenever the outcome of this race was mentioned." He went on to say: "But today, tonight, we can turn that 'inshallah' into 'alhamdulillah'. For the right-wing ops, that just means 'praise be to God.'" Republicans unable to win by distancing from Trump The defeat of Susan Collins, who has served as the Republican senator for Maine for three decades, was one indicator of the scale of the Republican losses. She was felled by Democratic candidate Troy Jackson, a logger who sought to point to his background to persuade blue-collar Mainers to vote for him. In a statement reported by US media, Collins conceded defeat and said it had been the "honour of my life" to serve the state for 30 years. The BBC's Helena Humphrey described a sombre atmosphere at Collins's watch party in the city of Maine - where the song Closing Time was played. Collins entered the race as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election, and found that her tactic to distance herself from Trump did not work. Ashley Hinson suffered the same fate in Iowa, losing that closely-fought Senate seat to Josh Turek. Hinson had slightly distanced herself from the president, urging him to end the war with Iran and breaking with him on easing beef tariffs, while at the same time defending Trump's broader tariff policies as important. History made by new black governors, first openly gay male senator and first Gen Z congresswoman Among the other firsts of the night were in Florida, where Republican Byron Donalds has become the state's first black governor, following a hearty endorsement from Trump. Donalds, who will take over the job from Ron DeSantis, said his state was the "envy of the nation", and that he would work to make the state more affordable. The result was one of the few high points of an otherwise difficult evening for the Republicans. In the neighbouring state of Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former mayor of Atlanta, won the governor's race, becoming the first black governor and first woman to be elected to the state's highest office. The BBC's Carl Nasman described ecstatic scenes as the race was projected blue. Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson, a billionaire businessman and healthcare executive. The state has also not had a Democratic governor for more than 20 years. Elsewhere, Democrat Chris Pappas became the first openly gay man elected to the Senate. He celebrated on stage alongside his husband in New Hampshire. Pappas defeated former Republican Senator John Sununu in the race, whom he thanked on Tuesday, saying: "We all owe John Sununu a big debt of gratitude for his public service for the people of New Hampshire." In Colorado, Melat Kiros became the first woman elected to Congress from Gen Z - meaning those who were born between 1997 and 2012. news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets

news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.summary: ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı ekimde 86 bin kişi artarak 67 bin kişilik piyasa beklentisini aştı. İstihdam artışının 82 bini hizmet sektöründen geldi.

news.titleTr: ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı beklentileri aştı: Ekimde 86 bin kişilik artış
news.summaryTr: ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı ekimde 86 bin kişi artarak 67 bin kişilik piyasa beklentisini aştı. İstihdam artışının 82 bini hizmet sektöründen geldi.
news.articleText: ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı beklentileri aştı: Ekimde 86 bin kişilik artış - ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı ekimde 86 bin kişi artarak 67 bin kişilik piyasa beklentisini aştı. İstihdam artışının 82 bini hizmet sektöründen geldi. ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı ekimde 86 bin kişi artarak piyasa beklentilerinin üzerinde gerçekleşti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ADP Araştırma Enstitüsünün, Stanford Dijital Ekonomi Laboratuvarı (Stanford Lab) işbirliğiyle hazırladığı ekim ayına ilişkin Ulusal İstihdam Raporu yayımlandı. Buna göre, ABD'de özel sektör istihdamı ekimde 86 bin kişi arttı. Piyasa beklentisi, özel sektör istihdamının bu dönemde 67 bin kişi artması yönündeydi. Özel sektör istihdamında eylülde kaydedilen artışa ilişkin veri ise 90 binden 86 bine revize edildi. Ekimde istihdam artışı hizmet sektöründe 82 bin, üretim sektöründe 4 bin oldu. ABD'de 26 milyondan fazla özel sektör çalışanının bordro bilgileri kullanılarak hazırlanan ADP verilerine göre, yıllık temel ücret artışı ekimde aynı işte kalan çalışanlar için yüzde 3 olurken, iş değiştiren çalışanlar için yüzde 4,8 olarak kaydedildi. ADP Araştırma Enstitüsü Başekonomisti Nela Richardson, verilere ilişkin değerlendirmesinde, geçen ay her büyüklükteki işverenin işe alım yaptığını belirtti. Verilerin, iş değiştiren çalışanların daha yüksek temel ücretin yanı sıra ikramiyeler, fazla mesai ödemeleri ve daha uzun çalışma saatlerinin birleşimiyle yeni işlere yöneldiğine işaret ettiğini aktaran Richardson, bu çalışanların toplam kazançlarındaki artışın Mart 2024'ten bu yana en hızlı seviyeye ulaştığını söyledi.

news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Democrats won control of Congress as a CertiK executive warned the CLARITY bill was “likely dead.” In Europe, ZachXBT identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the suspected victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million. Democrats win Congress as CLARITY bill faces fresh doubts Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections, giving the party greater influence over crypto legislation and oversight of President Donald Trump’s administration. At the time of writing, Democrats had secured 228 House seats to Republicans’ 139, with 68 races still uncalled, according to the Associated Press. The Senate tally stood at 54 seats for Democrats and 44 for Republicans. The result could derail the CLARITY crypto market structure bill, according to Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK. “The immediate read on this election result is that CLARITY bill is likely dead,” he said in comments shared with Cointelegraph, referring to both the upcoming lame-duck session and the next Congress. Muehlbauer said he expected Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Maxine Waters, both outspoken crypto critics, to chair the Senate Banking Committee and House Financial Services Committee, respectively. Democratic control could also bring greater congressional scrutiny of Trump-linked digital asset businesses. ZachXBT identifies French bank as alleged victim of $133M crypto theft Onchain investigator ZachXBT has identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million, warning that total losses could be higher. On Wednesday, the pseudonymous crypto sleuth said the institution, which he described as having $235 billion in assets, was allegedly exploited over multiple days. He also suggested that additional losses may have occurred through over-the-counter (OTC) transactions that were not included in earlier estimates. “I suspect the amount stolen is larger when accounting for OTC activity,” ZachXBT said. The bank’s alleged involvement has not been independently verified, and ZachXBT has not disclosed how the attackers gained access to the funds. The disclosure follows ZachXBT’s initial report on Monday, when he identified over $106 million in suspicious withdrawals from centralized exchanges. On Tuesday, he raised the estimated losses to over $133 million after discovering another $27 million in withdrawals, some of which occurred after his initial warning.

news.title: ABD Hazinesi'nden 125 milyar dolarlık tahvil ihracı kararı
news.summary: ABD Hazine Bakanlığı, kasım ayında vadesi dolacak borçların yeniden finansmanı kapsamında toplam 125 milyar dolarlık tahvil ihraç edeceğini açıkladı. İhaleler yoluyla piyasalardan yaklaşık 28 milyar dolarlık yeni kaynak sağlanması hedefleniyor.

news.summaryTr: ABD Hazine Bakanlığı, kasım ayında vadesi dolacak borçların yeniden finansmanı kapsamında toplam 125 milyar dolarlık tahvil ihraç edeceğini açıkladı. İhaleler yoluyla piyasalardan yaklaşık 28 milyar dolarlık yeni kaynak sağlanması hedefleniyor.
news.articleText: ABD Hazinesi'nden 125 milyar dolarlık tahvil ihracı kararı - ABD Hazine Bakanlığı, kasım ayında vadesi dolacak borçların yeniden finansmanı kapsamında toplam 125 milyar dolarlık tahvil ihraç edeceğini açıkladı. İhaleler yoluyla piyasalardan yaklaşık 28 milyar dolarlık yeni kaynak sağlanması hedefleniyor. ABD Hazine Bakanlığı, kasım ayına ilişkin borçlanma programının ayrıntılarını duyurdu. Bakanlık, 15 Kasım 2026'da vadesi dolacak yaklaşık 97 milyar dolarlık borcun yeniden finansmanı için toplam 125 milyar dolarlık tahvil ihracı gerçekleştirecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Planlanan ihraçlarla özel sektör yatırımcılarından yaklaşık 28 milyar dolarlık ilave finansman sağlanacak. Üç farklı vadede tahvil ihraç edilecek Açıklamaya göre, borçlanma programı kapsamında 58 milyar dolarlık 3 yıl, 42 milyar dolarlık 10 yıl ve 25 milyar dolarlık 30 yıl vadeli tahvil ihraç edilecek. İhale takvimine göre 3 yıl vadeli tahviller 9 Kasım Pazartesi, 10 yıl vadeli tahviller 10 Kasım Salı ve 30 yıl vadeli tahviller 12 Kasım Perşembe günü satışa sunulacak. İhalelerin tamamı Türkiye saatiyle 21.00'de gerçekleştirilecek. Tahvillerin takas işlemleri ise 16 Kasım Pazartesi günü tamamlanacak. Finansman ihtiyacı farklı araçlarla karşılanacak ABD Hazinesi, yılın son çeyreğinde kalan finansman ihtiyacını karşılamak için düzenli borçlanma araçlarını kullanmayı sürdürecek. Bu kapsamda haftalık bono ihaleleri, nakit yönetimi bonoları ve aylık tahvil ihraçlarının yanı sıra enflasyona endeksli tahviller (TIPS) ile 2 yıl vadeli değişken faizli tahviller de kullanılacak.

news.articleText: İstanbul Sanayi Odası Başkanlığı seçimlerini Adnan Dalgakıran kazandı - İstanbul Sanayi Odası Başkanlığı seçimlerini Adnan Dalgakıran kazandı. Adnan Dalgakıran 86, Ender Yılmaz 67 oy aldı. Çelik İhracatçıları Birliği (ÇİB) Başkan Vekili Mustafa Tecdelioğlu, İstanbul Sanayi Odası (İSO) Meclis Başkanlığı'na seçildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İstanbul Sanayi Odası Başkanlığı seçimlerini Adnan Dalgakıran kazandı. Adnan Dalgakıran 86, Ender Yılmaz 67 oy aldı. İstanbul Sanayi Odası (İSO) seçim sürecine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunan Adnan Dalgakıran, odanın geleceğine yönelik yeni bir vizyon ortaya koymak için çalışacaklarını belirtti. 'Geleceğe yönelik yeni bir vizyon koymak için çaba sarf edeceğiz' Dalgakıran, İSO'nun köklü tarihine yakışır bir seçim süreci geçirdiklerini ifade ederek, "Geleceğe yönelik yeni bir vizyon koymak için çaba sarf edeceğiz." dedi. Dünyanın hızlı bir değişim içinde olduğuna dikkati çeken Dalgakıran, kurumların da bu değişime ayak uydurması gerektiğini vurguladı. Dalgakıran, "Biz de değişmek zorundayız, dünya hızlı değişiyor. İSO'da 21. yüzyıla yakışan bir organizasyon yapacağız." ifadelerini kullandı.

news.title: France backs reporting for self-custodied crypto worth 100K euros or more
news.summary: The amendment would require taxpayers to report holdings worth at least $112,000, but the measure still needs to survive the budget process.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: France backs reporting for self-custodied crypto worth 100K euros or more
news.summaryTr: The amendment would require taxpayers to report holdings worth at least $112,000, but the measure still needs to survive the budget process.
news.articleText: France backs reporting for self-custodied crypto worth 100K euros or more The amendment would require taxpayers to report holdings worth at least $112,000, but the measure still needs to survive the budget process. The French National Assembly approved an amendment that would require taxpayers to report self-custodied crypto holdings totaling at least 100,000 euros ($112,000) to tax authorities. Amendment I-2701 was adopted on Tuesday in a 150–44 vote, with eight abstentions, according to the Assembly’s official voting record. The threshold would be assessed on Dec. 31 of the relevant tax year. Separately, the Assembly rejected an amendment that would have exempted gains on crypto payments for goods and services from tax if the payments totaled no more than 1,000 euros ($1,120) during the tax year. The proposal was defeated 69–14, according to the Assembly’s transcript. The reporting requirement forms part of the 2027 Finance Bill and would need to be retained in the final legislation to become law. The Assembly faces a Nov. 17 deadline to complete its first reading of the bill. Senate debate is scheduled to begin Nov. 20, according to its schedule. Crypto measures await final budget approval The National Assembly postponed Tuesday’s scheduled vote on the budget’s revenue section for the second time as lawmakers continued debating amendments. The vote was originally scheduled for Oct. 20. The vote’s postponement itself does not introduce a significant change, but the “likely rejection” of the budget’s revenue section could “result in the rejection of the entire bill in the National Assembly, including provisions adopted by way of amendments,” Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph. On Friday, the Assembly rejected two proposals that would have applied exit taxes to unrealized crypto gains when taxpayers transferred their tax residence abroad. Lawmakers also approved an amendment on Oct. 16 that would tax gains from converting crypto into stablecoins. The proposal covers stablecoins classified as electronic money tokens under EU rules and would still need to be retained in the final law. Related: French Senate adopts bill for automatic sharing of crypto tax data

news.title: Elon Musk's millions fail to deliver Texas for the Republicans in fierce midterms
news.summary: The billionaire's political action committee (Pac) contributed $47m (£35m) to Ken Paxton's campaign.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Elon Musk's millions fail to deliver Texas for the Republicans in fierce midterms
news.summaryTr: The billionaire's political action committee (Pac) contributed $47m (£35m) to Ken Paxton's campaign.
news.articleText: Elon Musk's millions fail to deliver Texas for the Republicans in fierce midterms - Published Democrat James Talarico's resounding victory in the Texas Senate race caused a major upset in the midterms for Republicans - and for Elon Musk. According to the Financial Times, external, the billionaire's political action committee (Pac) contributed $47m (£35m) to Republican candidate Ken Paxton's campaign, on top of the $158m he gave the Senate Leadership Fund in September. The money was not enough to stop the seat from turning Democrat for the first time since 1988. In his acceptance speech, Talarico said: "We just proved that all the money in the world is no match for the people of Texas." "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time," Musk jokingly wrote on X, external. Talarico's victory marked a key turning point in the midterms, helping solidify the Democrats' control of the US Congress in a wave of wins across the US. Musk has increasingly made Texas the hub of his companies, from Tesla's Austin headquarters to SpaceX's Starbase launch site. As well as backing Paxton through outside groups, the X owner took to his own platform to spread conspiracy theories about the Democrat, posting: "There is something deeply wrong with Talarico" after he briefly disappeared from the campaign trail in October. "There is something deeply wrong with a political system that allows one trillionaire to buy his own personal US Senator," Talarico posted in response. On top of contributing to one of the most expensive Senate races ever, the SpaceX owner also became the top individual donor in this year's midterms overall, contributing an estimated $446m in backing Republican candidates. Musk's money went through Super Pacs, groups which can raise unlimited sums but can't give directly to candidates or coordinate with their campaigns. Individuals, parties and traditional groups face legal limits on direct donations. Super Pacs get around this by spending independently, such as on ads backing a candidate. Musk became one of the Republican Party's biggest donors in 2024, pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into Donald Trump's winning presidential campaign. A similarly eye-watering amount was not enough to do the same for Paxton this time around. Sign up for our Tech Decoded newsletter to follow the world's top tech stories and trends. Outside the UK? news.title: ABD seçimleri Musk'ın şirketlerini vurdu: Tesla ve SpaceX hisselerinde sert düşüş
news.summary: ABD ara seçimlerinde Demokratların Kongre'nin iki kanadında da kontrolü ele geçirmesinin ardından Elon Musk'ın şirketleri Tesla ve SpaceX'in hisselerinde düşüş yaşandı.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: ABD seçimleri Musk'ın şirketlerini vurdu: Tesla ve SpaceX hisselerinde sert düşüş
news.summaryTr: ABD ara seçimlerinde Demokratların Kongre'nin iki kanadında da kontrolü ele geçirmesinin ardından Elon Musk'ın şirketleri Tesla ve SpaceX'in hisselerinde düşüş yaşandı.
news.articleText: ABD seçimleri Musk'ın şirketlerini vurdu: Tesla ve SpaceX hisselerinde sert düşüş - ABD ara seçimlerinde Demokratların Kongre'nin iki kanadında da kontrolü ele geçirmesinin ardından Elon Musk'ın şirketleri Tesla ve SpaceX'in hisselerinde düşüş yaşandı. - Yatırımcılar, yapay zeka düzenlemelerinin sıkılaşması ve iki şirketin olası birleşmesinin daha fazla incelemeye tabi tutulması ihtimalini değerlendiriyor. ABD'de ara seçimlerde Demokratların Kongre'nin kontrolünü ele geçirmesinin ardından Elon Musk'ın sahibi olduğu Tesla ve SpaceX'in hisseleri geriledi. Yatırımcıların yapay zeka sektöründe düzenlemelerin sıkılaşabileceği ve iki şirket arasında olası birleşmenin zorlaşabileceği endişeleri satış baskısını artırdı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Al Jazeera'nın haberine göre, Tesla hisseleri çarşamba günü piyasa açılışı öncesi işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 5 düşerken, SpaceX hisseleri önceki kapanışına kıyasla yüzde 6,9 geriledi. Her iki hisse de ilerleyen işlemlerde kayıplarının bir bölümünü telafi etti. Demokratların özellikle Teksas'ta elde ettiği başarı, Tesla ve SpaceX'in merkezlerini bu eyalete taşıyan Musk açısından da dikkat çekti. Musk, seçim sürecinde Cumhuriyetçilere destek vermiş ve Demokratlara oy verilmemesi çağrısında bulunmuştu. Yapay zeka düzenlemeleri ve birleşme endişesi First New York'tan Vikram Rai, Demokratların seçimlerdeki başarısının iki şirketin yatırımcıları açısından çifte risk oluşturabileceğini belirtti. Rai, Demokratların Kongre'de kontrolü sağlamasının yapay zeka alanında daha sıkı düzenlemeler getirilmesi ve Tesla ile SpaceX arasında olası birleşmenin önündeki engellerin artması ihtimalini güçlendirdiğini ifade etti. ABD'li haber sitelerinin konuya yakın kaynaklara dayandırdığı haberine göre, iki şirket arasında bir anlaşmanın gelecek yılın ilk yarısında duyurulması ve Donald Trump'ın başkanlık dönemi sona ermeden tamamlanması yönünde girişimler bulunuyor. Birleşme ihtimali henüz araştırma aşamasında bulunuyor. Olası işlem, iki şirketin faaliyet alanları ve büyüklükleri nedeniyle düzenleyici kurumların incelemesine konu olabilir. Musk ise seçim sonuçlarının ardından X hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, uzayda veri merkezleri kurulmasının artık cazip bir seçenek gibi göründüğünü belirtti. Musk Cumhuriyetçilere 450 milyon dolar aktardı Haberde, Musk'ın seçim sürecinde Cumhuriyetçi Parti'nin finansmanına yaklaşık 450 milyon dolar katkı sağladığı ve X platformundaki 240 milyon takipçisine Demokratlara oy vermemeleri çağrısında bulunduğu aktarıldı. Tesla hisseleri, yapay zeka ürünlerine yönelik iyimser beklentiler ve SpaceX ile olası birleşme ihtimali sayesinde temmuz sonundaki dip seviyelerinden itibaren yüzde 34 yükselmişti. Haziran ayında halka arz edilen SpaceX ise dünyanın en değerli şirketleri arasına girmişti. Şirketin piyasa değeri yaklaşık 1,9 trilyon dolar seviyesinde bulunuyor. SpaceX ayrıca ABD hükümetiyle yaptığı sözleşmelerden milyarlarca dolar gelir elde ediyor. İki şirketin yapay zeka alanındaki faaliyetleri de olası düzenleyici incelemelerin odağında. Starlink'in askeri amaçlarla kullanılan versiyonuna erişim konusu ise ABD, Ukrayna ve Rusya arasındaki ilişkilerde gerilim yaratan başlıklardan biri olarak öne çıkıyor. Nationwide Funds Baş Stratejisti Mark Hackett, seçim öncesinde siyasi söylemlerin ve duyguların piyasalar üzerinde etkili olduğunu, seçimlerin ardından ise temel göstergelerin ve ekonomik gerçeklerin daha belirleyici hale geldiğini söyledi. Öte yandan Tesla ve SpaceX, ürün geliştirme çalışmalarına milyarlarca dolar harcamayı sürdürüyor. Ancak sürücüsüz taksi, insansı robotlar ve Mars'ta yerleşim gibi projelerin şirket gelirlerine anlamlı katkı sağlamasının önünde yıllar olduğu değerlendiriliyor.

news.title: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
news.summary: Some Republicans tell the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost them.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
news.summaryTr: Some Republicans tell the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost them.
news.articleText: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat - Published Inside the Republican Party, initial shock at the stunning election results on Tuesday night quickly gave way to anger with US President Donald Trump. After Democrats won upset after upset in deep-red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina, some Republicans focused their ire on Trump, arguing that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party control of Congress. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told the BBC. "This is a disaster of the first magnitude. Nobody saw it coming like this." Most Republicans expected to lose control of the House and were clear-eyed about the challenge of holding onto the Senate in a tough election cycle that favoured the party out of power. But some said in interviews that Trump dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington. "It was just one mistake after another," said Gregg Peppin, a Republican strategist in Minnesota. "Clearly, in state after state, people did not like the president's policies." A White House ally said public disapproval with Trump over the Iran war, tariffs and the administration's immigration crackdown created a "perfect storm" in November. "There's palpable frustration [within] the party about how this has all played out," the person said, and much of it is directed at Trump. Anger with Trump "is extremely high". The BBC spoke to a dozen party operatives, campaign officials, White House allies and others, many of whom spoke on background to offer a candid assessment of Trump's approach to the midterms. Trump and Republicans had a lot riding on the outcome on Tuesday night. A stronger showing by the president's party - as happened in 2022, when Democrats under then-President Joe Biden lost just nine seats in the House, and gained one in the Senate - would have given Republicans some momentum heading into 2028. But Trump will instead face a motivated Democratic majority in Congress that is eager to investigate the administration, block his judicial nominees and stymie the rest of his agenda. The midterms have ushered in an uncertain new phase in Trump's second term and may force Republicans to start grappling with their post-Trump future. "I don't think his influence is slipping," said Steve Scheffler, the Republican National Committeeman in Iowa, speaking on the eve of the election. Still, he said, when it came to the midterms, "there were things you wish he said differently". Trump was silent for much of the night before posting a message on Truth Social after the House and Senate were called for Democrats. "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter," Trump wrote. He said in later interviews with the New York Times and Fox News that he would accept the election results. Trump told Fox he was a "little bit surprised" by the election results, but noted that the president's party typically fared poorly in midterm elections. Since 1934, the party in the White House has only gained seats in three midterm elections. While the Democratic gains in 2026 did not set a record, the party did win dozens of House races, state governor contests and Senate seats, including in states where the party had not been competitive for decades. Before Tuesday, Democrats had not won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, and had not won a statewide race in Texas in more than three decades. The party also notched surprise upsets in other reliably red states like South Carolina that were thought to be safe seats for Republicans just weeks before Election Day. Trump and Vice-President JD Vance held dozens of campaign rallies in the run-up to the midterms. The principal Trump-aligned Super PAC, MAGA Inc., spent hundreds of millions backing Republican candidates. Trump allies said it was unfair to hold him responsible for the party's election losses. They pointed to the history of midterm elections, and said the party was saddled with weak Republican candidates in battleground states like Georgia, Michigan and Texas. Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate nominee in Texas, ran "the worst Senate campaign in the country from either side of the aisle," said another Texas Republican operative, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. "If Ken's campaign knocked on 100,000 doors I'd be shocked," the source said. The person added that Paxton's victorious Democratic opponent, James Talarico, ran "a really good and smart campaign." Others defended Trump's autumn campaign schedule, noting that he had to balance his day job of running the country with midterm travel. "He's the president. He's not going to spend his time campaigning 24/7," said Krish Mathrani, the Michigan Republican Party's youth chair. Mathrani said Trump's campaign rallies helped drive up enthusiasm among Republican voters. "President Trump is a turnout machine," he said. That's true in presidential elections. But Trump's vaunted turnout operation has failed to deliver in elections when he's not on the ballot, and 2026 proved no different. Voters rejected Trump's argument that the economy was better on his watch and that he was achieving his aims in the war with Iran. The effort by Trump to portray Democrats as extreme socialists also fell flat, as voters handed victories to moderates like Roy Cooper in North Carolina. "That just didn't work with Cooper," said a Cooper campaign official. "Trying to tag him as some socialist liberal, that wasn't going to fly." Trump often seemed disinterested in the midterms over the summer, the period of time when Republicans in Congress shifted their focus to the election. Trump was consumed by the war with Iran abroad and his construction overhaul of Washington at home. The projects included the under-construction ballroom and a helipad on the South Lawn of the White House, renovations to a local golf course, a proposed memorial arch near Arlington Cemetery and renovations to the Kennedy Center. Events like a UFC match at the White House on Trump's 80th birthday in June created the impression that the president was more interested in feting himself than winning the midterms, several sources said. Trump also repeatedly downplayed the rising costs of gas and often cast the affordability issue as a Democratic hoax. Trump turned his full attention to the election in September at the Republican Party's midterm convention. The event was a gamble: Republicans hadn't held a midterm convention in decades, and it was an open question whether voters would tune in. Trump dominated the convention in Dallas, frustrating Republicans who told the BBC they wanted to highlight the party's midterm candidates. In his rambling keynote speech, Trump pledged to give $5,000 (£3,700) to anyone who voted for Republicans and raised eyebrows with an endorsement of Paxton which included a lengthy criticism of the candidate's lack of charisma and physical appearance. After Democrats won upset after upset in deep-red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina, some Republicans focused their ire on Trump, arguing that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party control of Congress. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told the BBC. "This is a disaster of the first magnitude. Nobody saw it coming like this." Most Republicans expected to lose control of the House and were clear-eyed about the challenge of holding onto the Senate in a tough election cycle that favoured the party out of power. But some said in interviews that Trump dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington. "It was just one mistake after another," said Gregg Peppin, a Republican strategist in Minnesota. "Clearly, in state after state, people did not like the president's policies." A White House ally said public disapproval with Trump over the Iran war, tariffs and the administration's immigration crackdown created a "perfect storm" in November. "There's palpable frustration [within] the party about how this has all played out," the person said, and much of it is directed at Trump. Anger with Trump "is extremely high". The BBC spoke to a dozen party operatives, campaign officials, White House allies and others, many of whom spoke on background to offer a candid assessment of Trump's approach to the midterms. Trump and Republicans had a lot riding on the outcome on Tuesday night. A stronger showing by the president's party - as happened in 2022, when Democrats under then-President Joe Biden lost just nine seats in the House, and gained one in the Senate - would have given Republicans some momentum heading into 2028. news.titleTr: Google'dan Malezya'ya 15 milyar dolarlık yatırım: 37 bin kişiye istihdam
news.summaryTr: Alphabet bünyesindeki Google, 2027 ve 2028 yıllarında Malezya'ya toplam 15 milyar dolar yatırım yapmayı planlıyor. Dijital altyapı, temiz enerji ve su projelerini kapsayan yatırımın, ülkede her yıl 37 binden fazla istihdamı desteklemesi bekleniyor.
news.articleText: Google'dan Malezya'ya 15 milyar dolarlık yatırım: 37 bin kişiye istihdam - Alphabet bünyesindeki Google, 2027 ve 2028 yıllarında Malezya'ya toplam 15 milyar dolar yatırım yapmayı planlıyor. Dijital altyapı, temiz enerji ve su projelerini kapsayan yatırımın, ülkede her yıl 37 binden fazla istihdamı desteklemesi bekleniyor. ABD merkezli teknoloji şirketi Google, Malezya'daki yatırımlarını büyütme kararı aldı. Alphabet bünyesinde faaliyet gösteren şirket, 2027 ve 2028 yıllarında ülkeye toplam 15 milyar dolarlık yatırım gerçekleştireceğini açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Yatırımın dijital altyapının genişletilmesi, yerel yeteneklerin geliştirilmesi ve temiz enerji ile su projelerinin desteklenmesi amacıyla kullanılacağı bildirildi. Malezya ekonomisine yıllık 1,1 milyar dolar katkı Google'ın açıklamasına göre, yatırım kapsamında inşa edilecek kampüslerin yapım sürecinin önümüzdeki iki yıl boyunca Malezya ekonomisine önemli katkı sağlaması bekleniyor. Kampüslerin inşaat sürecinin Malezya'nın gayrisafi yurt içi hasılasına (GSYH) yıllık ortalama 1,1 milyar dolar katkıda bulunacağı öngörülüyor. Projelerin ayrıca her yıl 37 binden fazla istihdamı desteklemesi bekleniyor. Google'ın planladığı yatırım, dijital altyapı ve kampüs inşaatlarının yanı sıra yerel iş gücünün geliştirilmesi ve sürdürülebilir enerji projelerine de odaklanıyor.

news.summaryTr: Tennis great Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of Spanish football giants Real Madrid.
news.articleText: Nadal set to join Real Madrid board of directors - Published Tennis great Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of Spanish football giants Real Madrid. Nadal won 22 Grand Slam titles, two Olympic gold medals and helped Spain claim five Davis Cups before retiring in 2024. Real's members will be asked to approve the 40-year-old's appointment to the board at a meeting later this month. In a statement announcing the move, external, the club said Nadal was "one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world". "It is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our board of directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club," Real added. The tennis legend - a boyhood Real fan who holds member's number 67,778 - included a photo of himself as a child in a club kit in his response to the news. "I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board for proposing that I join the board of directors of Real Madrid," Nadal said in his post on X, external. "I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can." It is currently unclear as to what responsibilities Nadal would hold on the club's board. Perez was re-elected to serve a new four-year term as Real president in June, having held the office since 2009. He swiftly appointed Jose Mourinho to a second spell as head coach, hoping to improve the club's fortunes after they went a second season without a trophy in La Liga, the Champions League or the Copa del Rey. Real are currently third in the league after 11 games - three points behind defending champions Barcelona. - Published28 August

news.articleText: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in three European nations - Published Needles and other sharp metal objects have been found in sweets handed out over Halloween in Germany, Austria and Hungary, prompting police to issue warnings to parents to check what their children have been given. Police in a number of German states have reported cases, from Bavaria in the south-east to Lower Saxony in the north. A girl aged nine hurt her tongue while eating a chocolate bar in Bremervörde, west of Hamburg. A 5cm-long (2in) pin was then found inside it. Meanwhile, police in Hungary have launched a criminal investigation after nails, screws and pieces of wire were found in sweets handed out to children who had been trick-or-treating in and around the town of Gyömrő, to the east of Budapest. The local authority said one young girl had been handed a toffee with a nail inside a chocolate wrapper and that she had fortunately noticed in time and had not swallowed the sweet. Several cases have also been reported across Austria, where Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as "cowardly, malicious and in some cases life-threatening". Police there said investigations were under way in four states, and that a 10-year-old girl had suffered a minor injury to her mouth when she bit into a small chocolate bar in the Amstetten area to the east of Linz. Lower Austria Governor Johanna Mikl-Leitner said the perpetrators had to feel the full force of the law, adding: "Our children deserve a carefree childhood and we'll continue to ensure that." - Warning after 'metal pins' found in Halloween sweets - Published9 hours ago German police in the south-eastern state of Bavaria said that, while there had been similar cases reported in the past two years, initial figures this year suggested a significant increase in incidents. As many as 25 cases involving sweets containing needles, screws or nails have been reported by police in Bavaria. Police in the Middle Franconia region of western Bavaria have also warned of the risk of copycat actions, after a mother found a needle in her child's chocolate bar and reported it to police. She later returned to the police to say her child had admitted to inserting the needle. - Published31 October 2023

news.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
news.summary: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.

news.titleTr: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
news.summaryTr: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.
news.articleText: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war' - Published Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans have "said NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections. "We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X. "If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned. Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices. But he insisted that he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran in February. Iran's Supreme Leader said he did not expect US policy to change after the results. Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the Iran war began, released a statement saying anyone who thinks there will be any change from American "hostility towards the Iranian nation" is "gravely mistaken". In an interview with Fox News, Trump said of the midterm results: "I think a part of it was Iran". He went on to say: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that." Speaking separately to the BBC's US news partner, CBS News, Trump said the conflict would end "when I say it ends". In recent weeks, the president has warned that the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran. Also on Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said four oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said two of the vessels were still burning, and two additional tankers had been intercepted, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. It said they were trying to travel through a prohibited southern route in the Strait of Hormuz. BBC Verify has been investigating the IRGC claims, and has not found any evidence that four tankers were destroyed. In a separate incident, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre said a tanker was struck by two unknown projectiles about 14 nautical miles (26km) north-east of Limah, in Oman's Musandam peninsula, on Tuesday evening. No casualties were reported, it added. On Monday, an Indian crew member of a dhow - a wooden sailing boat - was killed in an attack north-east of Limah. Thirteen other crew members were rescued by Omani authorities. The IRCG also reported on Wednesday that its forces had shot down another US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz. It made a similar claim on Monday night, when US officials said the US military had carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft. - US midterms: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night - Published8 hours ago In an interview with the Financial Times ahead of the midterms, Trump suggested he was happy with the state of the conflict, and that he did not consider them to be "really in a war". When asked about what the newspaper described as "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack on Iran this week, Trump said they were "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no need for it". Indirect talks to end the conflict have been stalled for months. President Masoud Pezeshkian maintained on Tuesday that his government had been trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue". "No-one will benefit from this war" if it were to resume, he warned. He also emphasised that Iran's supreme leader had granted the government powers to negotiate "issues that he had previously considered off-limits". Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqai said on Monday that the basis of the current indirect negotiations mediated by Qatar remained a seven-step proposal that Iran submitted in September. But he added that the proposal had been "condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days". The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, was effectively closed after the start of the Iran war due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and the US naval blockade. The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade. Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters. To keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the Strait of Hormuz. Additional reporting by Gabriela Pomeroy Related topics - Published1 day ago

news.title: Poundland owner in crunch talks as retailer's collapse looms
news.summary: Gordon Brothers will meet Jonathan Reynolds on Wednesday as the investment firm faces scrutiny over Poundland.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Poundland owner in crunch talks as retailer's collapse looms
news.summaryTr: Gordon Brothers will meet Jonathan Reynolds on Wednesday as the investment firm faces scrutiny over Poundland.
news.articleText: Poundland owner in crunch talks as retailer's collapse looms - Published Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds will meet the US-based owners of Poundland on Wednesday as the government hopes to save the retailer from collapse. The discount chain is on the brink of insolvency and Gordon Brothers, which bought it for £1 last June, has rejected a takeover bid which could have saved the 12,000 jobs currently at risk. A meeting was due to be held on Thursday but has been brought forward as the scramble to secure a rescue deal for the firm intensifies. Gordon Brothers has previously said Poundland faces multiple economic challenges from rising inflation, increasing staff costs, and "severe levels of shoplifting". Both Reynolds and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have questioned why a deal for the future of the business has not been made. Meanwhile, MPs say they have called in Poundland's owners for questioning to explain their role in the discount retailer's looming insolvency. Liam Byrne, chair of Parliament's business committee, said: "Every report suggests Poundland is a viable, profitable business with a future ahead of it and without good reason to let it crash and burn - and then to break it up and sell it off piece by piece. "We are asking Gordon Brothers to appear before Parliament to explain themselves and tell us just what it is that's preventing them from accepting the fully-funded deal on the table to save more than 12,000 jobs." Business Minister Kate Dearden and union representatives are also meeting Poundland's managing director Barry Williams later today. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its lenders until next Thursday. The meeting comes after a major Poundland supplier has said it will lose millions of pounds if the retailer goes bust. Adam Turner, sales director at Bradford-based Highcrest Retail Brands, said Poundland was one of its biggest customers and its collapse would cost it "a few million" in lost sales. The family owned business mainly sells confectionery to Poundland and turns over about £50m. Turner said the firm becoming insolvent would leave a substantial gap in its balance sheet next year. Highcrest was a "longstanding business that can stomach this", Turner said. But he warned other medium and small suppliers to the retailer have told him that "if Poundland goes under, so do they". This echoes a warning from Poundland founder Steve Smith on Monday that two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, which only work for Poundland, would be directly affected by its collapse. Not only would Poundland's 12,000 staff be affected in that case, but potentially up to 30,000 overall, he told the BBC on Wednesday. He said he was "amazed" Poundland was being put into administration, pointing to the profitability of the company. "Also, there's two offers on the table from some really good people," he added. "All I'm asking is for Gordon Brothers to see if they can put a deal together." Gordon Brothers said Walsall-based Poundland is "still not cash generative at a sustainable level" because of the economic issues it faces. If Poundland's stores are sold to new buyers, some of the employees may get new jobs on the same premises. However, it is understood that buyers are only interested in about half the stores at present – meaning roughly 6,000 employees would not be re-employed. - Poundland's founder offers to invest in firm - Published2 days ago High stock levels If Poundland goes under, suppliers will be getting "pennies in the pound" back from the administration, he said, which is "very upsetting" – although he still hopes a deal can be done so Poundland can remain solvent. Poundland owners Gordon Brothers will be a secured creditor, which means they are first in line to get their money back, and suppliers "who have done nothing wrong" will take the financial hit. "It's sad. It's a nightmare for us all to be honest with you. It's not just the suppliers, it's the staff at Poundland, some of these guys have been there for many years. "It's from the warehouse staff all the way to the shop staff to everybody within head office. It's a massive ripple effect through the supply chain," he added. Turner said he had no knowledge of whether Gordon Brothers had deliberately timed the process of Poundland going into administration so it could take advantage of having high stock levels, which it can then sell. One of the ways Gordon Brothers makes money is through stock liquidations – selling off stock from collapsed businesses. One insider familiar with the situation told the BBC that the timing of Poundland facing collapse was "odd" – most retailers don't fall over in the run-up to Christmas. Ministers' questions Dearden has said the government doesn't want to interfere with "current ongoing commercial negotiations", but that ministers want "clarity" on the plans for the retailer. "It's absolutely legitimate for this government to ask the business if they're doing everything they can to protect employees and suppliers up and down the country," she added. Dearden told MPs that the government would be ready to help the company's employees if Poundland collapses. The head of Gordon Brothers' European operations reportedly told the government that the firm stood by its stewardship and had given Poundland £85m in additional financing since its purchase in 2025. news.title: Canton’s CC rises 4% as SEC staff view it as ‘digital commodity’
news.summary: SEC staff’s no-action letter covers CC earned by running infrastructure and applications, but is not a binding ruling on its legal status.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Canton’s CC rises 4% as SEC staff view it as ‘digital commodity’
news.summaryTr: SEC staff’s no-action letter covers CC earned by running infrastructure and applications, but is not a binding ruling on its legal status.
news.articleText: Canton’s CC rises 4% as SEC staff view it as ‘digital commodity’ SEC staff’s no-action letter covers CC earned by running infrastructure and applications, but is not a binding ruling on its legal status. Canton Network’s native cryptocurrency rose 4% on Wednesday after the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) Division of Corporation Finance issued a no-action letter stating it views the token as a “digital commodity.” Canton Coin (CC) traded at $0.098 at 10:27 am UTC, but was still down roughly 4.2% over the past week, according to CoinMarketCap. Canton Network is a privacy-focused network that enables banks and financial institutions to tokenize assets, trade and settle transactions across different platforms. In its Tuesday letter, SEC staff accepted the explanation that CC’s value comes from how the network operates and demand for the token, rather than a central team’s efforts to generate profits for holders. The division also said it would not recommend enforcement action over CC’s issuance without securities registration, provided the tokens are created under the conditions described by Canton. In Friday’s letter to the SEC, Canton developer Digital Asset said network participants earn CC by operating infrastructure and applications, with the protocol determining how many tokens they can mint based on their activity. The SEC issued guidance in March distinguishing digital commodities, such as Bitcoin and Ether, from securities. It said these tokens are not themselves securities, although the way they are offered and sold can still be subject to securities laws. The SEC’s response reflects its staff’s position and is not a binding ruling on CC’s legal status. SEC staff previously issued token-related no-action letters to crypto projects, including DoubleZero (2Z) in September 2025 and Solana-native decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) project Fuse in November 2025. Related: NEAR token sinks 7% as proposal to cut annual token issuance passes

news.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
news.summary: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
news.summaryTr: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.
news.articleText: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline - Published South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC). This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes. Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations. Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection. For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. The party had a disastrous showing in the last national election, when it lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since 1994 when the racist apartheid system ended. Support for the party has been dropping significantly over the years because of anger over high levels of corruption, unemployment and crime. At its peak, in 2004, the ANC got 70% of the vote in the general election. Two decades later its share dropped to 40%. Polls and pundits have predicted a further loss in these elections but President Cyril Ramaphosa has denied that his party was in a downward spiral. "What I'm seeing here is that the ANC is going higher and higher and on the 4th [of November] we will show those naysayers," he told supporters at the party's final election rally on Sunday. In townships like Alexandra, north-east of Johannesburg, the ANC has traditionally had a strong supporter base but poor governance and voter apathy are unravelling this support. The BBC visited the sprawling township a week before the elections and spoke to residents to get their views. One of them was Sanele Ntombela, who is a first-time voter excited to make his voice heard. We found the 18-year-old hanging out with his friends on a street corner. Most of his friends said they had no intention of voting and had not registered to do so. They cited a lack of change and deteriorating delivery of basic services. But Ntombela was looking forward to voting for the first time and thought it might lead to change. "We face many challenges in Alexandra. There's rubbish everywhere and we struggle with electricity and water and many other issues," he said. Just metres away, heaps of rubbish lay gathered beneath a streetlight pole covered in election posters from the different political parties. On the other side of the street, drain water trickles through the many potholes that have gutted that part of the road. The BBC also spoke to Zandile Mncube, who said she wouldn't vote, even though she is registered to do so. The 33-year-old woman also cited poor service delivery and performance by local leaders for her decision. "It makes no difference [whether I vote or not]. Things have gotten worse over the years," she said. Alex, as the township is known, is a stone's throw away from Sandton, Africa's richest square mile, but the differences could not be starker. Sandton is known for its skyscrapers, designer shops and well-maintained roads but in Alex, houses are sandwiched together and rubbish, either piled together or left strewn across the pavement, is everywhere. The stench of raw sewage and uncollected rubbish is heavy in the air, but residents appear used to it. The issues plaguing Alexandra are not unique. A drive around Gauteng province reveals similar patterns of neglect and disrepair, especially in the townships. South of Johannesburg, Soweto looks marginally cleaner than Alexandra, but residents also complain about service delivery. Mduduzi Makhubo, 45, has lived in Soweto his entire life and he told the BBC of the community's daily struggles with accessing water and electricity. "Every Monday we know we won't have water after 2pm," he said. Makhubo is registered to vote and intends to use his vote to deal with the "arrogance" he says local leaders have towards residents and "change the status quo". These areas offer a small, but important, glimpse into the state of South Africa's local governance. Years of reports by the auditor-general have highlighted the dire state of most of South Africa's 257 municipalities. A recent report only gave 39 clean audits - the highest ranking a public entity can achieve - between 2024 and 2025. None of Gauteng's three metro cities, Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni, featured in this list. Earlier this year auditor-general Tsakani Maluleke said Johannesburg "needs ongoing attention". "If we don't that, we are going to continue on this slide where financial health deteriorates [and] where service delivery continues to be compromised, which is what we are living," she told lawmakers. The city has been labelled "effectively bankrupt" due to the dire state of its finances. Dirty streets, unstable electricity supply and persistent water issues have been common for years. Experts the BBC spoke to agreed that all eyes will be on Africa's wealthiest city as well as the country's seven other biggest municipalities, or metros, particularly those in Gauteng when the results come in. In Gauteng, all three metros are governed by coalition governments, with the ANC the largest party. But that might change. Political analyst Melanie Verwoerd said the elections would be a "verdict ... and judgment" on the ANC. "And the expectation is that the ANC generally in the country is going to [perform] the worst it's ever done," she said. One, conducted by Ipsos, put the ANC's support at 30%, down from the 46% it got at the last local elections in 2021. Ipsos predicts the DA will garner 25% support in this election, up from 22% last time. The former Cape Town mayor has been captured swimming in crater-sized potholes, ziplining over sinkholes and riding into her final rally in the city in a classic BMW 325i, known locally as a "Gusheshe". She believes the DA is the country's best choice for a government, telling local radio broadcaster 702 last week that "towns and cities that work best are under DA governance". Verwoerd, a former ANC MP and South Africa's ambassador to Ireland, predicted that coalitions would continue being the order of the day across Gauteng. These types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic at a local level and the constant change in leadership, usually caused by parties falling out with each other, has affected service delivery in many municipalities. Verwoerd said in her view, the most stable coalitions would be those that replicate what the ANC and DA have done on a national level, where the historic rivals have agreed to share power. Reflecting on Cape Town, she said it was unlikely that the DA would lose control of the municipality. The coastal city is widely considered the country's best-performing metro and has been run by the DA since the late 2000s when it unseated the ANC. Ethekwini, which includes the port city of Durban in KwaZulu-Natal, would be a "different story", Verwoerd said. The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has been projected to perform well in the area but it is unclear if it will secure the outright majority needed to run the metro. Polls suggest it won't and will need partners to form a government. The party was founded by former South African President Jacob Zuma and was the biggest party across his home province of KwaZulu-Natal in the 2024 provincial election. Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations. For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern. news.summary: Zach Pandl highlighted institutional custody safeguards as crypto markets recovered some losses following the record $6.3 billion Binance hack.

news.titleTr: Binance hack may be ‘temporary setback’ for crypto, Grayscale’s Pandl says
news.summaryTr: Zach Pandl highlighted institutional custody safeguards as crypto markets recovered some losses following the record $6.3 billion Binance hack.
news.articleText: Binance hack may be ‘temporary setback’ for crypto, Grayscale’s Pandl says Zach Pandl highlighted institutional custody safeguards as crypto markets recovered some losses following the record $6.3 billion Binance hack. Binance’s $6.3 billion hack could temporarily hurt confidence in crypto markets but would ultimately lead to stronger security practices across exchanges, according to Grayscale. “It also underscores the importance of institutional custody, such as offered by US-based crypto [exchange-traded products],” said Grayscale’s head of research, Zach Pandl, in a Tuesday report. “These vehicles hold their assets at state-chartered banks and qualified custodians, typically offering offline storage, multi-signature wallets, SOC attestations and insurance policies,” he added. Binance suffered a record $6.3 billion hack Thursday and pledged to cover all customer losses. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea. Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the allegations as “absurd rhetoric.” The hack was followed by a market sell-off, with Bitcoin falling below $77,000 and BNB losing more than 8% over 24 hours by early Friday. By Wednesday, total crypto market capitalization had rebounded 2% over the past 24 hours to about $2.63 trillion, after touching a weekly low of about $2.55 trillion earlier in the day. The recovery left the market about $100 billion below its Oct. 28 level. Bitwise’s head of research, André Dragosch, told Cointelegraph that recent outflows from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds were “related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment.” Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis

news.titleTr: Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure
news.summaryTr: Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10.
news.articleText: Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10. Tron founder Justin Sun is seeking $263,821.20 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial and its lawyers, accusing the Trump family-linked crypto company of submitting a misleading court disclosure about its ownership in a legal dispute over his $45 million WLFI token investment. In a federal court filing, Sun and two co-plaintiffs alleged that World Liberty initially listed Florida as its sole citizenship before amending its disclosure nearly three months later to identify 22 individuals and entities in its ownership chain, including those in the United Arab Emirates. “World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were,” Sun said. “When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.” The amended disclosure came six days after a federal judge questioned World Liberty’s bid to move Sun’s claims into arbitration. World Liberty’s lawyers subsequently argued that the company’s UAE citizenship deprived the federal court of jurisdiction because foreign parties were on both sides of the lawsuit. World Liberty Financial did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for comment. Related: Circle shareholder sues Trump, World Liberty and Steve Witkoff over crypto deals In April, Sun sued World Liberty, alleging fraud and the unlawful freezing of his tokens. World Liberty filed a defamation lawsuit against Sun in May, alleging false statements and violations of token-sale terms. Sun denied the allegations. The legal back-and-forth followed a January 2025 agreement by an Abu Dhabi-backed investment vehicle to purchase a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million. Sun previously backed the Trump family’s crypto ventures by investing in World Liberty and buying President Donald Trump’s TRUMP memecoin. He topped the token’s leaderboard for a May 2025 dinner with Trump, with holdings valued at about $18.5 million. UAE ownership disclosure prompts jurisdiction dispute In an Aug. 26 email included in the court exhibits, World Liberty’s lawyer Sam Cleveland said his team had “recently” learned of additional citizenship information. He maintained that World Liberty already had UAE citizenship when Sun filed the lawsuit in April. Sun’s lawyers subsequently sought corporate records and testimony about World Liberty’s ownership and when its attorneys learned of the UAE connection. They allege that World Liberty provided limited documentation but declined to explain why its original disclosure omitted that information. According to attorney Edward Moss’s sworn declaration, the $263,821.20 request covers fees for four attorneys’ work opposing arbitration. It excludes other lawyers’ fees and costs related to jurisdictional discovery and the sanctions motion. Sun said Tuesday he plans to refile in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is scheduled for Dec. 10. news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-
